text: US stock and bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving, and trading in gold, oil and currencies overseas is thinner than usual.
Spot gold eased to about $3,564 by 7:55 AM ET, about 0.7% below Wednesday's close, after bouncing from a 15-month low the day before.
Silver rose about 1% to roughly $41.5, so the gold/silver ratio fell to about 86 from 87.3.
Brent edged up to about $94.71 early Thursday, a third straight gain, as Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and mines hit tankers near Hormuz.
The yen firmed slightly to about 159 per dollar in Tokyo ahead of Tokyo inflation data due tonight, which feeds the Bank of Japan's December decision.
The dollar index was nearly flat near 103.7 in the holiday lull.
Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000, to about $60,621, up roughly 3% over 24 hours.
